raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The Kimi-K3 KDA MTP verify kernel (`fused_kda_decode_mtp_dspark`) spends much of its time on precompute dependencies and state synchronization. Rebalancing that work cuts kernel latency by up to 1.37× on B300, and outputs stay bitwise identical.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/kda_decode_mtp.py`:

- Keep convolution weights in producer registers, removing their shared-memory staging and the initial CTA barrier.
- Reorder independent convolution/gate work and prefetch output-normalization inputs using spare producer capacity.
- Use warp-level synchronization for warp-local state transfers, and overlap resident-state loads with precompute while keeping the cross-warp barriers.
- Public wrapper, launch dispatch, persistent AOT cache, ReplaySSM, padding, output normalization and caller-owned output buffers are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

B300 (SM103), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13, CuTe DSL 4.6.2:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_decode_mtp.py` and `test/registered/unit/layers/test_kda_decode_mtp_slot_stride.py`: pass on both main and this PR.
- **Bitwise identical to main**: 56 configurations (N ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}, H=12, num_spec ∈ {3, 7}, ReplaySSM ring on/off, fused output norm on/off). All 420 output tensors were compared (output, intermediate SSM/conv states, ReplaySSM rings, recurrent state), with 0 differences.
- `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck`: 0 hazards across 4 shapes covering ring/full-snapshot and norm on/off.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300, H=12, K=V=128, same process. **Warm** = per-call time from a CUDA graph of 50 back-to-back calls (median of 11 replays). **Cold** = in-graph `[512 MiB L2 flush, kernel] × 20` minus a flush-only graph (median of 21).

Speedup range (main → PR) across N = 1…64:

| Mode | num_spec | Warm speedup | Cold speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReplaySSM ring + output norm | 3 | 1.22–1.29× | 1.22–1.35× |
| ReplaySSM ring + output norm | 7 | 1.22–1.33× | 1.26–1.37× |
| ReplaySSM ring | 3 | 1.08–1.20× | 1.06–1.20× |
| ReplaySSM ring | 7 | 1.13–1.22× | 1.15–1.22× |
| Full snapshots + output norm | 3 | 1.10–1.15× | 1.10–1.24× |
| Full snapshots + output norm | 7 | 1.07–1.09× | 1.07–1.14× |
| Full snapshots | 3 | 0.98–1.04× | 0.98–1.04× |
| Full snapshots | 7 | 1.02–1.04× | 1.02–1.04× |

<details><summary>Per-shape timings (µs)</summary>

| N | num_spec | ring | onorm | warm main → PR | cold main → PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 6.145 → 4.957 | 10.246 → 8.195 |
| 8 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 6.636 → 5.448 | 11.368 → 9.326 |
| 64 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 28.467 → 22.626 | 41.830 → 31.890 |
| 1 | 7 | 1 | 1 | 9.544 → 7.701 | 14.854 → 10.954 |
| 8 | 7 | 1 | 1 | 9.951 → 8.028 | 15.658 → 12.083 |
| 64 | 7 | 1 | 1 | 47.864 → 36.065 | 59.347 → 45.515 |
| 1 | 7 | 1 | 0 | 8.767 → 7.701 | 12.898 → 10.856 |
| 64 | 7 | 1 | 0 | 43.233 → 36.394 | 56.371 → 47.266 |
| 1 | 7 | 0 | 1 | 17.080 → 15.692 | 21.405 → 18.843 |
| 64 | 7 | 0 | 1 | 98.303 → 91.483 | 101.325 → 94.934 |
| 1 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 9.216 → 9.052 | 12.184 → 12.288 |
| 8 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 9.705 → 9.872 | 13.107 → 13.270 |
| 1 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 16.671 → 16.138 | 19.970 → 19.130 |
| 64 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 93.554 → 91.459 | 97.227 → 95.179 |

</details>

The full-snapshot, no-norm path is roughly neutral (worst case 0.98× at N ≤ 8 with num_spec = 3, within run-to-run noise). The production ReplaySSM path gains 1.06–1.37×. On Vera Rubin (SM107) the production case (N=1, num_spec=7) drops from 13.2 µs to 9.7 µs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Existing KDA MTP tests cover the kernel.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
